docs.text: BagaCAD Draw edges, close faces and extrude directly in Blender. 0.22 Alpha · Blender 5.2+ This is a short working manual. The addon is still in development; save a copy before testing. Install Open Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions . Use the menu > Install from Disk… and select the BagaCAD ZIP. Enable the extension. Disable older development copies first. Start drawing F3 > BagaCAD New Drawing creates an empty mesh. F3 > BagaCAD Draw works on the active mesh. Both commands are also in N > BagaCAD . Click points to draw. Close a flat contour to make a face. Right-click to start another chain. The viewport header shows the current action. Drawing · Extrusion · Dimensions · Shortcuts Scope BagaCAD edits the active mesh. Other objects can hide snap targets but are not themselves snap targets. Hidden mesh elements are ignored. X-Ray and Wireframe allow snapping to revealed geometry. Non-planar contours stay open. Complex geometry is not guaranteed to work. Dimensions and their locks are temporary tool data, not a persistent CAD constraint system.

docs.text: Dimensions Press D , then click an edge. A single selected or active edge may be picked automatically. Labels show the edge length, nearby parallel distances and angles. Change a value Click a label: type a replacement. Drag a label horizontally: adjust the value. Ctrl while dragging: use increments. Shift while dragging: move ten times more finely. Enter / click: confirm typed input. Releasing a drag confirms it. Esc / right-click: cancel the edit. Ctrl + A replaces the whole value; Ctrl + V pastes. Lengths accept units such as mm , cm , m , ft and in . Angles use degrees. Fixed end and locks Outside input, press Tab or click the support icon to switch the fixed endpoint. Hover a value to reveal its padlock. Click it to lock or unlock that dimension. Locked values are kept while neighboring geometry adjusts. If constraints conflict, cancel or unlock a value. Locks last only while Dimensions is active. Leaving this mode clears them. Return to drawing D / Esc , outside input, returns to drawing. Right-click deselects the edge. Ctrl + Z or Backspace , outside input, undoes a validated change.

docs.text: Draw Click to place a start point, then click to add segments. Right-click to start a new chain. On a face: use Ctrl + click , away from guides, to start drawing instead of extruding. Precision X / Y / Z: lock an axis. Press again to release. Shift + X / Y / Z: lock to YZ / XZ / XY while drawing. Press again to release. Type a length, press Tab , then type an angle. Tab switches between the two fields. Click / Enter: confirm the typed segment. Backspace: correct the input. Esc: clear it. A length fixes the distance but lets the direction follow the mouse. An angle fixes the angle but lets the length change. Enter both to fix both. Snap targets include vertices, midpoints, edges, faces, guides and grid nodes. With a fixed length, aiming at a snap target chooses the direction while keeping that length. Hold Alt to suspend automatic inferences; mesh and grid snaps remain available. Faces Close a flat contour to fill it. Draw between face borders to cut a face. Crossings split edges; overlapping segments merge. To fill a missing flat region, retrace one of its border edges. Existing coplanar faces are not covered. A diagonal across an empty square can fill both sides. Undo and finish Ctrl + Z undoes a validated change; during a guide transformation it cancels the preview. Backspace , outside numeric input, also undoes the last geometry change. Esc cancels the current setup/input or selection, otherwise exits the tool. Enter , with no input or selection pending, also exits. Orbit, pan and zoom remain available. The numpad enters numbers during a segment; before the first point it keeps its view shortcuts.

docs.text: Extrude Hover inside a face, with no segment in progress. Click the highlighted face, move the mouse, then click again or press Enter . Type a distance for an exact result. Negative values move in the opposite direction. Esc / right-click cancels the preview. Several faces Shift + click: add or remove a face from the selection. Release Shift, then click a selected face, or press Enter , to extrude the selection. Alt + click: extrude the connected coplanar faces instead; this replaces the manual selection. For non-coplanar selected faces, the whole group moves in one direction: the normal of the last selected face. Esc / right-click , before extrusion starts, clears the selection. Snapping Aim at a vertex, midpoint, edge or face to match its height along the extrusion direction. Hold Alt during extrusion to disable this snap. A typed distance takes priority. Result Outward extrusion can fuse with volumes in the same mesh. Inward extrusion can make a pocket or a through-hole. The exact boolean calculation happens when you confirm. An isolated surface keeps a bottom and becomes a volume. Other objects remain separate.

docs.text: Guides & grid Guides Hover to acquire a reference. A short hover stores a temporary reference; a longer hover creates a persistent guide. Vertex or midpoint: an XYZ reference. Edge interior: an infinite construction line. A on a vertex, then click another vertex: a guide through both. Hold Ctrl over a guide: move it; release to confirm. Hold Shift over an XYZ axis: rotate that reference around its origin; release to confirm. Esc / right-click: cancel a transformation. R: remove the last guide. Shift + R: remove all guides and temporary references. Temporary references keep the two most recent acquired vertices/intersections. They provide axes, edge extensions and real 3D intersections. They clear after committing a segment or starting a new chain. Grid Shortcut Action G Show or hide the remembered grid Shift + G Place or reorient it in two clicks Ctrl + G Set cell size by measurement or typing Alt + G Place and align it to the hovered face Shift + X / Y / Z Set a world grid to YZ / XZ / XY, with no segment active For placement, click an origin, then a direction. Esc / right-click cancels the setup. The grid snaps to line intersections, not cell centers. Its default step is 0.1 Blender unit. Showing or hiding it preserves current numeric input.

docs.text: Shortcuts & settings These are the current defaults, not the proposed future keymap. Action Shortcut Draw / confirm / extrude a hovered face Left click, depending on context Draw on a face Ctrl + click, away from guides Select extrusion faces Shift + click Extrude connected coplanar faces Alt + click New drawing chain / cancel preview Right click Dimensions / return to drawing D, outside input Axis lock X / Y / Z Plane lock while drawing Shift + X / Y / Z Length / angle input Tab Undo geometry Ctrl + Z Delete digit / undo geometry outside input Backspace Cancel current input/setup, otherwise finish Esc Confirm input/selection, otherwise finish Enter Suspend drawing inferences Hold Alt Grid G; Shift/Ctrl/Alt + G for setup Guide through two vertices A, then click Move guide / rotate XYZ reference Hold Ctrl / hold Shift over guide Remove last guide / all guides R / Shift + R Preferences Open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > BagaCAD . Setting Default in the current source Create Guide Timer 2.0 s Edge Guide Delay 2.0 s Temporary Vertex Delay 0.15 s Temporary Intersection Delay 0.15 s Grid Step 0.1 Blender unit Length Snap Step 10 cm Angle Snap Step 15° The length and angle increments apply to Ctrl-dragging dimensions. Display Text controls labels near the cursor. Leave Debug Mode off for normal use. Saved preferences can differ from these defaults. Hover delays are already editable; a complete custom keymap editor is not implemented in this version.
